title: KVO-LLM: Boosting Long-Context Generation Throughput for Batched LLM Inference
problem: Long-context LLM inference with batching incurs extreme external memory access (EMA) from KV cache; modern accelerators suffer PE under-utilization due to low arithmetic intensity, while existing KV compression trades accuracy for efficiency.
motivation: Long-context models are critical for RAG and reasoning, but KV cache dominates memory traffic in batched inference, creating a memory-compute bottleneck.
method: KVO-LLM accelerates batched LLM inference by coupling algorithm and hardware optimization. The algorithm reduces KV cache size through quantization that prioritizes tokens important to attention (salient tokens), followed by pruning of KV channels and tokens based on attention patterns. The hardware uses a multi-core accelerator with operator fusion (combining operations to reduce memory transfers) and cross-batch interleaving (mixing requests to maximize processor and DRAM bandwidth utilization). This works because smaller data volumes mean less memory pressure and more opportunities to keep processors busy.
key_novelty: The core novelty is co-designing the algorithm (quantization and attention-guided pruning of KV cache) and hardware architecture (operator fusion and cross-batch interleaving) as a single integrated system.
contributions: Reduces KV cache EMA by >91% with significant accuracy advantages over prior KV compression
Up to 7.32x throughput improvement vs. state-of-the-art LLM accelerators
limitations: Not discussed; scalability to very long contexts (>100k tokens) and multi-model batching unclear.
primary_theme: KV cache optimization for long-context LLM batched inference
